content: The combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF interacts with various drugs by altering their metabolism, primarily through inhibition of hepatic and intestinal enzymes such as CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, as well as affecting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transport. These interactions can lead to increased plasma concentrations of the affected drugs, potentially resulting in serious or life-threatening adverse effects. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for monitoring or modifying therapy: 1. Beta-blockers (e.g., betaxolol, carvedilol): Plasma levels are increased due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and patients closely monitored for adverse effects. 2. Bortezomib: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 3. Bosentan: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dosage adjustments are necessary. 4. Brexpiprazole: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Administer half the usual dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a CYP2D6 inhibitor is also used, reduce the dose to one-quarter. 5. Bromocriptine: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Budesonide: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 7. Buprenorphine (all formulations): Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for signs of toxicity or overdose, especially when transitioning between formulations. Adjust therapy as needed. 8. Bupropion: Levels are increased by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Buspirone: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 10. Busulfan: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 11. Calcifediol and Calcitriol: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially altering vitamin D metabolism. Monitor serum vitamin D, PTH, and calcium levels, and adjust calcifediol dose as needed. 12. Calcium carbonate: Decreases levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 13. Capreomycin, Carboplatin, Cisplatin, and Colistin: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Captopril: Levels are increased via CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Carbamazepine: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Celecoxib: Levels are decreased via CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Chlorpromazine and Clomipramine: Levels are increased via CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Chlordiazepoxide, Clonazepam, and Diazepam (all formulations): Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider dose reduction of benzodiazepines and monitor for adverse effects. 19. Chloroquine: Levels are increased via both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 20. Ciclosporin: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition, and co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cilostazol: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 22. Citalopram: Levels are increased via both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 23. Clarithromycin: Levels of both clarithromycin and cobicistat may increase. Reduce clarithromycin dose by 50% if CrCl < 60 mL/min. 24. Colchicine: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not co-administer if renal or hepatic impairment is present. Adjust colchicine dose as needed. 25. Conivaptan: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Contrast media (iodinated): Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Crizotinib: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 28. Cyclophosphamide: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Dabigatran: Levels are increased via P-gp inhibition. Avoid co-administration if CrCl < 30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or < 50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 30. Dantrolene: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 31. Dapsone: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition and decreased via CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Darifenacin: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Dasatinib: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Deflazacort: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose. 35. Desipramine: Levels are increased via CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 36. Dexamethasone: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 37. Digoxin: Levels are increased via P-gp inhibition. Initiate digoxin at a low dose and titrate carefully. 38. Diltiazem: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Disopyramide: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Docetaxel: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 41. Doxepin: Levels are increased via CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 42. Doxorubicin (all formulations): Levels are increased via both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 43. Dronabinol: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Dronedarone: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 45. Diflunisal and Diclofenac: Co-administration increases toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Darunavir: Levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Dapsone: Levels are increased via CYP3A4 inhibition and decreased via CYP2C9 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of careful monitoring and dose adjustments when co-administering elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with other medications.
